name: 作业与考试
description: Assignments and exams: the api/assignments + api/exams surface (14 routes), lifted out of api/modules/learning as its first slice (P4.3b.5b). These two services were the only Prisma-free part of that domain - plain SQLite over four tables - so they could move on their own. Adopts the two parents and their two child tables; reads students only to expand a class into one grade row per pupil and to label the grade sheet.

data._adopted_note: All four keep their legacy names because `SELECT *` rows are the HTTP contract: `reward_points`, `due_date` and `submitted_at` (assignments) and `total_score`, `exam_date` and `feedback` (exams) go straight to the frontend. Renaming them is the coordinated P7 namespace migration tracked by guardrail G10. The two child tables ship with their parents rather than becoming separate plugins because neither has meaning without its parent, and `deleteAssignment`/`deleteExam` delete children-then-parent by hand (there is no ON DELETE CASCADE).
data._reads_note: Two uses, both read-only. `createExam` runs `SELECT id FROM students WHERE class_id = ?` to seed one empty `student_exams` row per pupil, inside the same transaction as the exam insert; `listGrades` joins `students` for `s.name` and the repository decrypts it with the host-supplied `config.decryptName`. No `dependsOn: classroom`: the classroom port exposes `listClassStudents` (which returns far more than the ids this needs) and `getStudentById`, and using either would create a startup dependency on a plugin whose absence changes nothing about these routes.
data._auth_note: All 14 routes are actor-guarded as of the route-authorization round (`docs/security/route-authorization-matrix.md`, the assignments table - every row of which was `无鉴权`). The controllers gate the role first (`src/assignments.authorization.ts`): 401 `未登录或登录已过期` for a request with no verified actor, 403 `无权限执行该操作` for a role the matrix does not list. The services then narrow what a permitted caller sees or writes: a teacher to the rows carrying their own `teacher_id` (the ownership anchor these tables store, and how 本班 is expressed here), a student to the class the kernel resolved for their login, a student/parent to their own `studentId` - a query naming another student or class is refused, never silently ignored. The ownership-gated writes (`PUT/DELETE /api/assignments/:id`, `PUT /api/assignments/student-assignments/:id`, `PUT /api/exams/:id*`, `DELETE /api/exams/:id`) resolve the row and refuse a teacher who does not own it. `teacher_id` on create is derived from the actor; a body copy is discarded. What remains, and what was deliberately not invented: '本班' is `assignments.teacher_id` / `exams.teacher_id`, not a `classes` lookup, because this plugin declares no read of `classes` and no `dependsOn: classroom` - so a teacher moved off a class still sees work they created in it. Two matrix rulings reach the UI: `GET /api/exams` is staff-only, so `StudentAssignmentsPage`'s exam-title lookup answers 403 for a student and the page falls back to `考试 #<id>` (its own default); and students/parents read `GET /api/assignments` scoped to their own class.
data._known_debt: api/modules/insights reads all four of these tables directly (class averages, assignment completion, per-student grade sheets) and api/modules/admin cascade-deletes from them. The admin path goes through Prisma `$transaction` rather than `DbApi`, so the ownership check cannot see it - see HANDOFF 8.3.1. When insights migrates it should consume a reporting port published here instead of declaring cross-domain reads; after this move that is the ONLY remaining reader.
